newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MANAGERS TO RESTART STEEL FIRM CLABECQ.
newsitem.headline: MANAGERS TO RESTART STEEL FIRM CLABECQ.

text.p: A Belgian court on Monday put company officials in charge of relaunching bankrupt steel maker Clabecq, taking some responsibility from the firm's receivers who were attacked by militants last week, Belgian radio said.

The latest project to restart activity at Forges de Clabecq SA, which was pronounced bankrupt in early January, was drawn up at the weekend by the three former company managers with the backing of trade unionists.

The plan proposed work for five months with guarantees of no social upset during that time, though it was unclear how the plan would be funded, Belgian media reported. Workers will vote on the plan on Tuesday.

Previously four court-appointed receivers had been in charge of restarting operations at the troubled steel firm and keeping it going while a partner could be found to take it over. Under the new plan, the managers would report regularly to them.
On Friday a group of trade union activists had burst into a meeting between the receivers and Clabecq managers and set upon the receivers.
One of the receivers, Alain Zenner, later appeared with heavily bruised eyes and cuts to the face.
Zenner said on Monday the problem was not finding a technically viable plan for Clabecq, which had been done previously, but finding the money to support it.

He added that Clabecq's banks and the Walloon region - the company's main share holder - had last week agreed to provide a total of 500 million Belgian francs, but that the current social climate might make them reluctant to hand it over.

"We have accords in principle from the Walloon Region and the banks for when a credible plan is produced - that is one where we can guarantee that (steel) activity continues positively and peacefully," he said.
Meanwhile a Brussels court of appeal earlier on Monday overturned a previous court order demanding that the four banks provide credit to Clabecq worth 650 million Belgian francs.

Roberto D'Orazio, militant leader of the socialist FGTB trade union and one of the workers implicated in Friday's attack, said at the weekend he was attacking a capitalist system which threatened 2,000 Clabecq families.
"The workers are not on strike, we are not occupying the plant. We have all been put out of work," he told Belgian television.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Deahene deplored the FGTB trade union's militant attitude, which he said was an "all or nothing approach, which will lead to nothing."
